claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **Not Eligible**

I'm sorry, but **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why this decision was made:

Alex is 20 years old, which means they fall outside the age criteria for Child Benefit. The rules specify that:

- Child Benefit is available for children **under 16**
- It can extend to young people aged **16-19** if they are in approved education or training
- Once a child reaches **20 years old**, they no longer qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes

### Important information:

If Alex was previously receiving Child Benefit, it would have stopped when they turned 20 (or at the end of the benefit year in which they turned 19, if they were in education).

**Note:** If you have a 16-17 year old who leaves education, Child Benefit can sometimes continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with a careers service or the armed services - but this doesn't apply in Alex's case as they are already 20.

### What you might consider:

While Child Benefit is not available, you may want to explore whether Alex or your household might be eligible for other forms of support, depending on your circumstances (such as Universal Credit or other benefits).

If you have any other questions or if there are other children in your household you'd like to ask about, please let me know!
